description: A magnificent UNESCO World Heritage Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, located in Thanjavur, built during the Chola dynasty.
history: Built by Raja Raja Chola I between 1010 CE, it stands as a prime example of fully realized Dravidian architecture.

description: A structural temple complex overlooking the Bay of Bengal, famous for its intricate rock-cut architecture.
history: Built in the 8th century during the reign of Pallava king Narasimhavarman II; designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

description: A sprawling hill fortress complex composed of three hillocks, often referred to as the 'Troy of the East'.
history: Built by the Chola dynasty and later fortified by Vijayanagara Empire, Marathas, and the French/British.

description: A popular tourist monument built on a small rock island off the coast of Kanyakumari, commemorating Swami Vivekananda.
history: Built in 1970 by the Vivekananda Rock Memorial Committee on the sacred rock where Swami Vivekananda meditated.

description: A historic Hindu temple located on the southern bank of the Vaigai River in Madurai, dedicated to Meenakshi and Sundareshwarar.
history: Rebuilt in its current form in the 17th century by the Nayak dynasty, featuring magnificent gopurams covered in colorful sculptures.

description: A Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva located on Rameswaram island, famous for its exceptionally long corridors.
history: Associated with the Ramayana epic; expanded significantly during the 12th century by the Pandya dynasty.

description: A famous Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva in his dancing form (Nataraja), located in Chidambaram.
history: An ancient temple with architectural contributions from Chola, Pallava, and Pandya dynasties, famous for its gold-plated roof.

description: A sprawling temple complex dedicated to Ranganatha (a form of Vishnu) located in Srirangam, Tiruchirappalli.
history: Considered the largest functioning Hindu temple in the world, built and expanded over centuries by various dynasties.

description: A national park and tiger reserve in the Nilgiri Hills, known for elephants, tigers, and diverse bird species.
history: Established as a sanctuary in 1940 and later declared a core part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve.

description: A protected tiger reserve located in the southern Western Ghats of Tamil Nadu.
history: Formally declared a tiger reserve in 2008, encompassing the former Indira Gandhi Wildlife Sanctuary.

description: A dense forest ecosystem and tiger reserve located in northern Tamil Nadu, known for rich wildlife and elephant corridors.
history: Declared a tiger reserve in 2011, spanning across the Sathyamangalam and Thalavadi ranges.

description: A marine national park consisting of 21 islands and coral reefs in the shallow waters of the Gulf of Mannar.
history: Established in 1986 to protect endangered marine species, coral reefs, and mangroves.

description: A mountain range spanning across Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka, famous for tea plantations and scenic beauty.
history: A historically significant British hill station cluster centered around Ooty and Coonoor.

description: A star-shaped artificial lake located in the hill station town of Kodaikanal, surrounded by lush green hills.
history: Created in 1863 by Sir Vere Henry Levinge, the then collector of Madurai.

description: A series of waterfalls on the Kaveri River where water splits into multiple streams, creating a smoky mist effect.
history: A prominent geological and tourist destination known for traditional coracle rides.

description: The second-largest mangrove forest in India, located near Chidambaram, offering intricate water channels.
history: A vital estuarine ecosystem formed by the Vellar and Coleroon river systems.

description: A historic meter-gauge rack railway operating steam locomotives through the Nilgiri Hills.
history: Built by the British in 1908 and designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site as part of the Mountain Railways of India.

description: A guided boat excursion through the dense, narrow waterways and canopy tunnels of Pichavaram Mangroves.
history: Eco-tourism initiative run to provide immersive nature viewing while supporting local fishermen.

description: An exciting traditional circular basket boat ride through the swirling rapids of Hogenakkal Falls.
history: An age-old local river navigation technique practiced by local boatmen on the Kaveri River.

description: A breathtaking vantage point at the southernmost tip of mainland India where the Arabian Sea, Indian Ocean, and Bay of Bengal meet.
history: Historically revered as a sacred confluence point (Triveni Sangam) and pilgrimage center.
